lore_anchors.definition: A Warring States-era school of strategic statecraft and persuasion. Practitioners specialized in building or breaking political coalitions, often acting as itinerant advisors and spies; in this novel, they serve as court counselors.

A malevolent entity whose pure malice corrupts host bodies physically (causing flesh to sag) and mentally (rewiring emotional baseline toward cruelty). Prolonged exposure rewrites personality entirely.

An eighth-rank military logistics officer responsible for cavalry supplies and horse management. Its real value lies in assignment to the Imperial Guard, granting access to the palace's power structure.
The emperor’s personal military corps—one of the Twelve Imperial Guard Corps. Assignment to this unit signals high trust and proximity to the throne.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Ji Lin change so completely?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He consumed Ling Xie and absorbed military killing intent to survive court politics—the old Ji Lin would have been killed quickly.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the School of Vertical and Horizontal Alliances?
cultural_notes_faq.a: An ancient Chinese school of statecraft focused on political alliance-making and persuasion; its members serve as advisors and schemers in court.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the Cavalry Aide a good position?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Its rank is low (eighth grade), but it places Li Huowang inside the Imperial Guard, giving him direct access to the palace’s military apparatus—it’s a strategic foothold.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Office hall empty?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The chapter does not explain yet, but the emptiness signals an event or shift—something has happened that Li Huowang has not yet discovered.
